symbols.name: number of cyclic coordinates
symbols.meaning: The number of cyclic coordinates of an array, a positive integer.
symbols.quote: Let $d$, a positive integer, be the number of cyclic coordinates of an array.

symbols.name: coordinate index
symbols.meaning: The index naming one cyclic coordinate, running from 1 to d.
symbols.quote:
Let $
u$ name one coordinate, running from $1$ to $d$, and let $\Lambda_
u$ be the cyclic length of coordinate $
u$, the number of positions along that axis before indices wrap around.

symbols.name: cyclic length
symbols.meaning: The number of positions along coordinate nu before its indices wrap around.
symbols.quote:
Let $
u$ name one coordinate, running from $1$ to $d$, and let $\Lambda_
u$ be the cyclic length of coordinate $
u$, the number of positions along that axis before indices wrap around.

symbols.name: last-axis position
symbols.meaning: An integer from 0 to r-1 giving a position along the last cyclic coordinate.
symbols.quote: Let $\kappa$ and $\kappa'$, integers from $0$ to $r-1$, be two positions on this axis.

symbols.name: second last-axis position
symbols.meaning: A second integer from 0 to r-1 giving a position along the last cyclic coordinate.
symbols.quote: Let $\kappa$ and $\kappa'$, integers from $0$ to $r-1$, be two positions on this axis.

relations.quote: A cyclic coordinate is one axis of a multidimensional [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), with its own cyclic length.
